overview: This one-page file contains a telegram sent from Bern on November 20, 1943, transmitting a summary from the Berlin Deutscher Reichsanzeiger of a Japanese press report on the wartime transformation of Japan’s textile industry. It describes the effects of the war with China, the embargoes imposed in July 1941, government controls, and adaptation to military production, and gives a percentage breakdown of the uses or disposition of Japanese textile mills as of May 1943, with some information corrected through August 1943.

people.name: Leland Harrison
people.role: U.S. Minister to Switzerland; sender of the telegram from Bern

subfiles.title: Telegram from Bern on wartime changes in the Japanese textile industry
subfiles.about: Reports a German newspaper’s summary of Japanese press information concerning the wartime disposition and conversion of Japan’s textile mills.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports that the Berlin Deutscher Reichsanzeiger of November 15 published information from the Japanese press on extensive changes in Japan’s textile industry since the outbreak of hostilities with China. The changes were intensified by the July 1941 embargoes and subsequent wartime developments and resulted from both government control and voluntary adaptation to war needs. The telegram provides a percentage breakdown of mills remaining in operation or being sold, leased, converted, merged, repurposed, held in reserve, consolidated, or used for unspecified purposes, based principally on their status in May 1943 and partly corrected through August 1943.

interest: The telegram offers a compact piece of Allied economic intelligence on the restructuring of Japanese civilian industry during the Pacific War. Its unusually detailed percentage breakdown is useful for studying industrial mobilization, the contraction of textile production, and the conversion of factory capacity to war-related uses. It is also an example of indirect wartime information gathering, in which a U.S. diplomat in neutral Switzerland relayed a German newspaper’s account of Japanese press reporting.
